title: bug: rollback restores the database BEFORE the version check, so a refused rollback has already moved bytes
description:
Filed 2026-09-09 by architect-ed42e60a from an external review (finding 2), VERIFIED at HEAD fee4e168: the reviewer's probe reproduced EXACTLY (Result EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT, database restore calls 1, docker calls 0) using the production handler and a recording restore port. Correctness refuter failed to refute. Severity refuter lowered it to MEDIUM: the risky arm (restoreDatabase:true + stale expectedVersion) is unreachable from the shipped browser -> daemon -> ports composition, host-operator-only, and the dump is recoverable — a bounded self-healing window plus a legibility gap, not unrequested destruction. Real, cheap, must land before real rollbacks are trusted.

MECHANISM (files byte-identical between 51c4a004 and HEAD):
- apps/daemon/src/deployment/rollback-command.ts:140-149 `if (request.restore && intent === null) { await applyRollbackRestore(...) }` — calls ports.restoreDatabaseInto (rollback-restore.ts:192) BEFORE the guard-parity read at :153-154 (IN_PROGRESS) and BEFORE the legs commit at :156-167 whose project leg (:161) carries `expectedVersion: envelope.expectedVersion`; a conflict there refuses at :165-167.
- The header :72-75 claims the version is checked "before any remote operation" — the opposite of the code. The :123-139 comment shows the placement was deliberate (task-b7cdf265, DONE, moved the arm from before the receipt guards to after them but still BEFORE the durable fences, conflating "read-only guards admitted" with "fences committed").
- rollback-command.test.ts:47 harness defaults restoreDatabase:false; the :68-93 version arm asserts only h.docker.calls with NO restore port wired; :223-225 envelopeFor always mints a FRESH expectedVersion so arms (a)-(d) never exercise a stale one. The ordering is unpinned.

UNDERSTATED BY THE REVIEWER: (1) the conflicted legs commit persists a NO_BUSINESS_EFFECT decision under the intent key, so the same commandId is then refused COMMAND_ID_SPENT and the only path forward is a new id — which applies the dump AGAIN (2 restores), violating the ONE-ATTEMPT invariant the code documents at rollback-restore.ts:173-176 and rollback-command.ts:132-135. (2) The same ordering fires for the environment guard: a second rollback submitted while one is in flight restores the dump mid-rollback and only then refuses IN_PROGRESS.

FIX SHAPE: split applyRollbackRestore (rollback-restore.ts) at the seam it already has: destination() + dumpToRestore() (:125-167) are pure reads, ports.restoreDatabaseInto (:192) is the effect. Export resolveRollbackRestore(config, environment) -> {databaseUrl, dump} | refusal, and applyResolvedRestore(resolved, ports). Keep the RESOLVE where :140 sits (pre-admission, so an unbound/unverifiable restore still refuses with nothing reserved, preserving arms (c)/(d)); move the APPLY to after :169 — inside the reserved guard, after the project expectedVersion leg has committed. On apply failure mint a REFUSED rollback receipt so the terminal commit at :206-213 releases the guard leg (the route test :435 already proves this for engine refusals) instead of stranding the environment IN_PROGRESS. Append an EnvironmentRollbackRestoreApplied event on the aggregateId stream between intent and terminal decision so the `intent !== null` recovery path (:170-183) can tell an applied restore from an unapplied one. A cheaper stopgap (hoist getAggregateVersion !== expectedVersion above :140) closes the exact probe but leaves a TOCTOU window against the concurrent project writers the :396 arm models — not sufficient alone. Fix the :72-75 header and :123-139 comment, which document the opposite of the code.

No open board row owns this. task-b7cdf265 (DONE) placed the arm; its DoD asserted only "a failing restore leaves the schema as it was", never "a refused admission leaves the port untouched". A malformed copy of this row (task-b70ac67a, empty description) was deleted minutes before this one was filed.
definitionOfDone: A boundHarness arm with restore:true and expectedVersion+1 refuses EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT with the restore port's calls toEqual([]) — the exact probe the review ran, now pinned, and its pre-fix RED (calls length 1) quoted in the completion record.
A second rollback submitted while the environment guard is held refuses IN_PROGRESS with ZERO additional restore-port calls.
A post-admission apply failure yields a REFUSED rollback receipt, the guard leg is released, and a fresh command is admitted — no environment stranded IN_PROGRESS.
A retry under a NEW commandId after a version conflict does not restore twice: the arm asserts total restore-port calls across both commands, pinning the ONE-ATTEMPT invariant the code documents.
The unbound/unverifiable-restore refusals (existing arms c and d) still refuse with nothing reserved, proving the resolve half stayed pre-admission.

The module header at rollback-command.ts:72-75 and the comment at :123-139 describe the actual ordering; the recovery path can distinguish an applied restore from an unapplied one via the new durable event.
pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test EXIT 0 with its count line quoted.

HEADER REWRITTEN, and the old text was wrong in a way that would have misled the next reader of this change. It said re-running would be "a second chance at an operation whose first outcome is already durable". A REFUSED apply is not durable: I verified backup-ports.ts runs psql with `--single-transaction` and `ON_ERROR_STOP=1` in one `docker run`, so a failure rolls the `DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE; CREATE SCHEMA public;` reset and the dump back together. The rule is now stated as ONE ATTEMPT PER ADMITTED COMMAND: a fresh command may resolve and apply again because that is a new admission; what may never be re-run is a SUCCEEDED apply, and that is fenced by the command's `intent === null`, not here — `applyResolvedRestore` cannot tell a first call from a second.

(a) RESOLVE STAYS PRE-ADMISSION under the unchanged `request.restore && intent === null` fence, now `resolveRollbackRestore(...)` into a `RollbackRestoreResolved | null`. Refusal forwards code, layer and detail exactly as before, so arms (c)/(d)'s "nothing reserved" and both production-wiring ENV_ENVIRONMENT_UNKNOWN@SCOPE arms stay green — verified, all 3 wiring arms pass.
(b) APPLY MOVED past `admitted.disposition === "REPLAYED"`, inside the reserved guard and after the project expectedVersion leg has committed.
(c) APPLY FAILURE commits a REFUSED TERMINAL under the command key: `{environment, outcome:"REFUSED", receiptId:null, refusal:{code,detail,layer}, restoreApplied:false, toReceiptRef}`, legs = Decided on the request stream at expectedVersion 1 plus Released on the guard at guardVersion, then rethrows the binding's own code@layer so the caller's answer is unchanged. An unrecorded apply refuses and holds the guard odd rather than continuing with an effect nobody can account for.
(e) MARKER IS LOAD-BEARING: the terminal request-stream leg is now `expectedVersion: restoreApplied ? 2 : 1`, so dropping the marker commit makes every restore:true rollback refuse at the terminal.
(f) `restoreApplied` is DERIVED FROM THE STREAM (`getAggregateVersion(aggregateId) === 2`) rather than from a local flag, which is what makes recovery work: a request admitted under the OLD ordering has no marker, reads version 1, and CONTINUES. It never refuses on a missing marker. REPLAY: `decided !== null && !recovered.ok` now decodes the terminal through a new shape-exact `refusedTerminal()` and rethrows the recorded code@layer; anything that is not exactly `{outcome:"REFUSED", receiptId:null, refusal:{code,detail,layer}}` still falls through to RECEIPT_INVALID. Header and the database-arm comment rewritten: they said the version is checked "before any remote operation", which was the opposite of the code, and now describe resolve-pre / apply-post, the refused terminal, the crash window, and the residual (psql commits, a later phase refuses, a fresh command re-applies the same dump and destroys any write landed in between).
